title: Savya

paragraphs: In Yevamot [16a](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.16a.17) and [16b](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.16b.3): “Rabbi Yochanan and Savya both say.” And there at [86b](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.86b.4): “Rabbi Yonatan and Savya disagree about it”; Hyman infers from the latter passage that Savya is a sage’s name.[^1][^2]

notes.text: Hyman lists Yevamot 16a and 16b separately; these are not asserted to be a continuous quotation spanning the folio boundary. His inference that Savya is a sage’s name is preserved as his inference; the William Davidson 86b paragraph has Yonatan and Savya disagreeing.

The linked passage at 16a has Rabbi Yochanan and Savya both saying the same thing. At 16b they disagree. At 86b Savya disagrees with Rabbi Yonatan. Hyman takes the last wording as evidence that Savya is the sage’s name.
